title: You’re not confused about dinosaurs.
paragraphs: You’re not confused about dinosaurs.
You’re wrestling with something deeper.
“Why doesn’t the Bible say what I expect it to say?”

And just like that—
we step out of curiosity…
and into confrontation.

Because if God is real—
He doesn’t answer to your categories.
He reveals Himself on His terms.

The word “dinosaur” is not in Scripture.
But don’t mistake silence for absence.

The Bible speaks of creatures that shake the ground,
that defy human control,
that humble kings and silence pride.
Behemoth.

“Look at Behemoth, which I made along with you…
what strength he has in his loins…
his tail sways like a cedar…” — Job 40:15–17 (NIV)
A tail like a cedar.
Pause there.

That’s not a small animal.
That’s not poetic fluff.

That’s something massive.
Something that makes man feel… small.
And then—
Leviathan.

Unstoppable. Untouchable.
A creature no man can tame.
And God asks Job:
“Can you pull in Leviathan with a fishhook?” — Job 41:1
Translation?

You can’t even handle creation…
what makes you think you can question the Creator?
But here’s what we miss.
We turn this into a debate about extinction, fossils, timelines.
Meanwhile, God is revealing something heavier:

Your limits.
His power.
Your need.
Because Job wasn’t asking about dinosaurs.
He was drowning in suffering.

He lost everything.
Wealth. Children. Health. Dignity.
And in the middle of his pain, he asked:
“God… where are You?”
And God didn’t give him a simple answer.
He gave him a revelation.
Not an explanation—
A confrontation with glory.
God points to creation and says:
Look at what I’ve made.
Look at what you cannot control.
Look at what you cannot understand.
And then ask yourself—
Do you really think I’ve lost control of your life?
That hits different.
Because suddenly this isn’t about ancient creatures anymore.

It’s about your anxiety.
Your unanswered prayers.
Your hidden fears.
You want God to explain everything.
But God wants you to trust Him.

“Where were you when I laid the earth’s foundation?
Tell me, if you understand.” — Job 38:4 (NIV)
That question still echoes today.
Where were you?

When He formed the oceans?
When He shaped the mountains?
When He designed creatures we still struggle to explain?
You weren’t there.
Neither was I.

And yet we demand answers
from the One who holds everything together.
But don’t miss the turn.
Because this same God—

The One who commands Behemoth.
The One who restrains Leviathan—
Chose the cross.
Let that sink in.

The God of overwhelming power…
stepped into human weakness.

“He was pierced for our transgressions,
he was crushed for our iniquities…” — Isaiah 53:5 (NIV)
This is where everything shifts.
Because the question is no longer:
“Are dinosaurs in the Bible?”
The real question becomes:
“Is your heart submitted to the God who made everything?”
Sin tells you:

“You need control.”
“You deserve answers.”
“You are the center.”
But the Gospel says:

You are not the center—
Jesus is.
And that’s not bad news.
That’s freedom.
Because if you’re not in control—
Then your failures don’t have the final word.
Your past doesn’t define you.
Your confusion doesn’t disqualify you.
Jesus steps in.
Not with condemnation—
But with a cross.

“For God so loved the world that he gave his one and only Son,
that whoever believes in him shall not perish but have eternal life.” — John 3:16 (NIV)
That includes you.
Yes, you.

The one with questions.
The one with doubts.
The one still scrolling, still searching.
You don’t need every answer.
You need a Savior.
And here’s the invitation:

Stop chasing explanations…
and start pursuing relationship.

Stop demanding control…
and start surrendering trust.
Because one day—

Every creature, every mystery, every question
will bow before Jesus Christ.

“At the name of Jesus every knee should bow…
and every tongue acknowledge that Jesus Christ is Lord.” — Philippians 2:10–11 (NIV)

From the largest creature ever formed…
to the smallest hidden fear in your heart—
He is Lord over all of it.
So what will you do with that truth?
Ignore it?
Debate it?
Or surrender to it?

This is bigger than dinosaurs.
This is about your eternity.
We don’t chase myths.
We follow the risen King.

From mystery to meaning—
because Jesus rewrites everything.
